newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts views on ABN AMRO's U.S. buy.
newsitem.headline: Analysts views on ABN AMRO's U.S. buy.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said it would offer $59 per share for Standard Federal Bancorp in a deal worth $1.9 billion. Analysts reactions follow.

"Selling MeesPierson and buying this bank with the proceeds looks like a good swap to me. ABN AMRO has a lot of experience with integrating new banks, especially in the field of back-office and automatisation systems. US banks are much cheaper than European ones, and the margins are very good.

"SFB has a margin of some 2.8 percent, well above ABN AMRO's which is below 2 percent. I am positive about it, but will not yet raise my forecasts. It usually takes a very long time for central authorities to give their approval. I think this will take at least six months, so it will be for the second half of 1997."

"My first reaction would be that it's a good fit for the operations in Michigan, Indiana, Ohio and Illinois. It's adjacent to, and partly overlapping, the areas where ABN has its main U.S. operations."

"It fits in with their strategy of remaining the leading player in (Illinois) and moving into to states adjacent to Illinois. It's a good, credible bank with good profitability. The (SFB share) price has moved up quite sharply. They have paid only a little over what it's been trading at in the last few days. They're paying about two times book (value), which is not exceptional."
"It looks good. It's a bank with quite good penetration. The takeover price doesn't seem to be expensive. It's not as expensive as when you buy a bank in Germany and France."

"It looks like they have quite a good funding base. The price to book (ratio) is about two times. You pay some goodwill because you pay for the whole operation. Maybe some things could be integrated with the Chicago activities (of ABN AMRO)."

"In principle I applaud the move. It's in line with ABN AMRO's strategy of international expansion. They are in the process of selling MeesPierson their Dutch subsidiary, that will free up some two billion guilders in capital. I read that they will issue $750 million in preference shares so that would about cover the acquisition price I think."

"They still have three acquisitions in the United States which still have to be approved by the U.S. regulatory authorities, these being Chicago Corp, Comerica Bank Illinois and Columbia National Bank. All three are of far lesser magnitude. They were more like sewing beads on a string, this is buying a whole necklace all at once. The only thing I wonder about is that it takes a long time for the U.S. regulatory authorities to approve the small acquisitions. I read that it's earnings enhancing and that's always nice. It seems that ABN AMRO is getting more dynamic in terms of divestments and acquisitions and that's a good thing."
